evals.prompt: can you write a jira ticket for this? support says trainers exporting the full pokedex get a csv that just stops, we have 1025 pokemon and one trainer only got 151 rows. been happening since at least last week, ~60 trainers/week hit it. repo is evals/fixtures/pokemon-service. don't push anything to jira yet, just give me the ticket
evals.expected_output: A Bug ticket in the bug template: symptom title, TL;DR, Impact with severity and the 60 trainers a week, numbered Repro, Expected 1025 rows and Actual 151, Acceptance Criteria with a regression test item. Agent notes name pokedex/export.py and MAX_ROWS = 151 as the suspected cause and give a verify command based on python3 -m unittest. It writes nothing to Jira.
expectations: Classifies the ticket as a Bug and uses Repro, Expected, and Actual sections.
Names pokedex/export.py and the MAX_ROWS = 151 slice as the suspected cause.
Gives a Verify command that runs the unittest suite, for example python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.
Has a Acceptance Criteria checklist with a regression test item that fails before the fix.
States the impact with the about 60 trainers a week figure.
Does not create or update a Jira issue.
Tags as [blocking] only questions whose answer changes the fix. A scoping detail such as which trainer store.all() returns is not [blocking].

evals.prompt: PM wants the pokedex list to get: filter by type, export only the filtered pokemon to csv, and saved teams per trainer. break it into tickets so we can hand them to a few coding agents at once. code is in evals/fixtures/pokemon-service
evals.expected_output: An Epic with a success measure, scope, and a Breakdown table of child tickets with types, dependencies, and lanes, plus one ticket file for each child. Tickets that edit the same file (pokedex/filters.py, pokedex/api.py) share a lane or have explicit dependencies. Saved teams gets a blocking question about storage, because the repository has no persistence for trainer data. Each child has Agent notes with verified paths and a Ready for an agent line.
expectations: Produces an Epic with a Breakdown table that lists each child with a Type, a Depends on value, and a Lane.
Produces a separate ticket for each of the three features: the type filter, the filtered export, and saved teams.
The lanes or dependencies stop two parallel tickets from editing the same file, such as pokedex/filters.py or pokedex/api.py.
Flags as a blocking open question, or as not ready for an agent, that saved teams need storage the repository does not have.
Each child ticket has Agent notes with a Ready for an agent line and paths that exist in the repository.
Reports which lanes or tickets can start in parallel now.
No ticket adds scope the request did not ask for, such as a new exception type, a latency target, or a metric.
Each child ticket delivers a behavior a person can verify end to end. No child covers only one layer, such as saved-team storage without the API that uses it.

evals.prompt: need a task ticket: move the nightly pokedex sync onto our redis queue so it stops blocking the api workers. repo: evals/fixtures/pokemon-service
evals.expected_output: A Task ticket. The validation surfaces that the repository has no Redis or queue code: the nightly sync in pokedex/jobs.py runs on a thread, so the premise is not verified. The ticket carries this as a blocking open question with an owner, sets Ready for an agent to no, and does not invent Redis paths or modules.
expectations: Classifies the ticket as a Task.
Points out that the repository has no Redis or queue code and that the sync runs on a thread in pokedex/jobs.py.
Adds a blocking open question with an owner about which Redis queue to use or whether it exists.
Sets Ready for an agent to no.
Does not name a Redis file, module, or class as if it exists in the repository.
Does not state as fact a runtime claim that the repository does not show, such as which process calls run_nightly_sync.

evals.prompt: POKE-42 is a mess, rewrite it in place. acli can't reach jira from this box so I dumped the issue with acli view --json to evals/fixtures/pokemon-service/POKE-42.json. code is in the same folder. give me the rewritten ticket and the exact commands you'd run once I say go
evals.expected_output: The ticket rewritten in the Story template, because trainers notice the sort, with the existing Jira type Task reported as a mismatch and not changed. The by-type sort is an open question, not a silent addition. The commands, not run, are in order: build the ADF comment from POKE-42.json with a Previous description heading, post it with acli jira workitem comment create, convert the ticket with md_to_adf.py, then acli jira workitem edit with a single-quoted summary and --description-file. No command removes the team-trainers or created-with-atlassian-mcp labels.
expectations: Rewrites the ticket in the Story template with an outcome title, TL;DR, Acceptance Criteria checkboxes, and Agent notes.
Reports that the template type (Story) differs from the Jira type (Task) and does not change the issue type.
Carries the by-type sort as an open question instead of adding it to Acceptance Criteria.
Lists a comment command that posts the old description with a Previous description heading before the edit command.
Lists an acli jira workitem edit command with a single-quoted --summary and a --description-file that points to ADF made by md_to_adf.py.
No command removes an existing label, and no command uses --remove-labels.
Does not claim that it ran any write command against Jira.
